name: Outbound reply gates: three switches that don't switch anything
description:
Found while investigating the rerun behaviour (CZ3TDR1-630), and unrelated to it. Three places where the tool looks like it is doing something and isn't — each one fails quietly, which is why none of them had been noticed.

- Turning **automatic replies off** for a partner in the admin has no effect. Replies keep being prepared exactly as before.
- When a reviewer **discards** a prepared reply, that partner comment can never be answered again. There is no error and no warning anywhere — the conversation simply goes quiet.
- A reviewer who has taken one pull request can act on a message belonging to **another partner's** pull request. This is a boundary between trusted internal users rather than a hole open to the outside, but it should hold.

**Done when:** switching automatic replies off actually stops them, a discarded reply leaves the reviewer a way to answer instead of silence, and any action a reviewer takes only ever touches the pull request they are holding.

Fixed in PR: https://github.com/shoptet/aidev-apps/pull/26

---

## Outcome (2026-09-10)

All three are fixed. Several things changed shape along the way and are worth recording, because they are promises to the team rather than implementation detail.

### The discarded reply works differently than this ticket assumed

The ticket asked for a discarded reply to be replaceable by a new prepared one. It is not, and deliberately so.

Preparing a reply again automatically turns out to need a decision we should not make in passing: a reply whose sending has permanently failed would then block any further attempt for good, with no way out. So the reviewer answers a discarded reply **by hand** — the console has always allowed that, and it now says so plainly instead of leaving the conversation to go quiet. The gap this ticket reported (silence, with no error and no route forward) is closed; an automatic redraft is a separate piece of work with that decision attached.

### Nothing a reviewer clicks can claim success it did not have

The investigation into the three switches turned up the same failure mode across the whole reply surface: when the tool refused to do something — the reply had already been sent, another reviewer got there first, someone had cancelled it — the console reported success anyway. The worst case took a reply a reviewer had written for a partner, cleared the box, said "Sent", and never sent it.

Every one of those now says what actually happened, and names which of it, so nobody goes looking in the wrong place. This was not in the original scope and is the larger part of the work.

### An empty reply could reach the partner

Two ways: a reviewer who cleared the draft's text box and approved it anyway, and an engine that answered with nothing usable. Either way the partner got a comment with no text in it, on their pull request, permanently — nothing between the click and GitHub looked at whether there was anything to send.

Both are closed now, and an engine that returns no text is treated as a fault: it raises an alert instead of quietly writing an empty draft. The same hole exists one column over, on findings rather than replies — a reviewer who clears a finding's text sends the partner a letter with a blank finding in it. That one is recorded in the code, not fixed here.

### An approved reply could get stuck with no way out

If the send failed to get queued — a database blip is enough — the reply stayed in a state that showed nowhere in the conversation and that Retry did not offer itself on. The reviewer was told it was approved and had no way to find out it would never go.

Such a reply is now recoverable from the admin Outbound log like any other failure, whichever way it got stuck. Retry does wait a while before offering itself, because a reply also looks exactly like this for the few seconds — or the length of a deploy — before a worker picks it up, and pressing Retry is not free: it adds a second send attempt rather than nudging the first.

### Two more switches that don't switch anything

The same pattern exists twice more. Both are behaviour changes to the sending path and both could stop releases that work today, so they are recorded rather than fixed here:

- The **release** cell in the admin matrix is decoration, exactly like automatic replies were. Setting it to "off" does not stop a reviewer's release. The admin page now warns about it.
- The **global kill switch** does not hold approved messages for later, as the admin page claimed. It lets them fail, with an alert, recoverable with Retry. The wording now describes that; the behaviour is untouched.

Also left for later, and recorded in the code:

- Making a second click on Retry genuinely impossible (today the second attempt is caught later in the pipeline, not prevented), and checking GitHub for an already-posted message on every send rather than only after a crash. Both change how sending behaves.

All of these are marked in the code and need their own ticket when someone picks them up.

### One thing to know about the release

Merging is the deploy. The new default for automatic replies takes effect immediately, which matters only for a partner whose switch someone had explicitly turned off — that switch starts working. Nothing else needs doing; while the tool is not answering partners for real there is nothing to check.
